# Test fixtures

**Everything here is synthetic.** No measured data, no research results.
See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) — this repository holds code and
specification only, and fixtures must be generated or from a published,
licence-compatible source.

## `example_zooms_spectra.parquet`

6 spectra, 18 columns, ~11 KB. Generated by
[`make_fixture.py`](make_fixture.py); regenerate with:

```bash
python tests/fixtures/make_fixture.py
```

Deterministic — the same seed produces the same bytes
(`sha256 aecb0f94…4f7f96`).

### What it illustrates

This is the worked example of what a **well-annotated** ZooMS table looks like,
and specifically of the three things the conformance audit found missing across
the real estate:

1. **Sample context columns** — `collection_name`, `provenance`, `plate`,
   `extraction_batch`. Most datasets have none of this.
2. **A CV-bound instrument** — `instrument_cv_id` / `instrument_cv_label`
   alongside the free-text `instrument`, so the value resolves to a PSI-MS
   term rather than being a string. This is the L0 → L1 step.
3. **File-level metadata** — the `zoomzpeak.*` key-value block that
   [Finding 3](../../docs/conformance_audit_2026-09-08.md) recommends every file
   carry: spec version, table kind, builder, CV reference. Read it with
   `pq.read_table(path).schema.metadata`.

### How the spectra were made

Each spectrum is built from **published COL1 collagen peptide marker masses**
(Buckley et al. 2009/2010; Kirby et al. 2013 and later literature) for one of
*Ovis aries*, *Capra hircus* or *Bos taurus*, plus a crude isotope envelope and
uniform background peaks. The marker masses are reference values from the
published record; everything around them is generated.

The peaks are therefore *recognisable* — which makes the fixture useful for
testing peak matching — but no spectrum here was measured from any object, and
the isotope model is illustrative rather than physical. **Do not use these
spectra to evaluate species-identification accuracy.**

### What it is modelled on, and what was withheld

The **structure** follows the richest real ZooMS dataset in the estate: the
relic-label corpus of **Crafting Documents, c.500–c.800 CE**, an AHRC-DFG funded
project launched in February 2023, led by Professor Julia Smith (University of
Oxford) in partnership with the Bundesanstalt für Materialforschung und -prüfung
(BAM), with co-investigators Professor Ira Rabin and Professor Oliver Hahn.

The project studies the transition between Late Antiquity and the Middle Ages
through parchment production, ink composition and penmanship, working on a
neglected corpus of roughly 500 relic labels — tiny documents, often only a few
centimetres long, originally attached to saints' relics. It asks whether
parchment-making and ink-preparation techniques changed across the period and
why, and what role relic cults played in transmitting artisanal knowledge
between generations.

That corpus is why this dataset has context columns the rest of the estate
lacks: a relic label *is* an archival object with a collection, a provenance and
a shelfmark, so the metadata had somewhere to go.

**Nothing from it is reproduced here.** Withheld deliberately:

- **Measured spectra.** All peak data is generated.
- **Archival shelfmarks.** `shelfmark` is present in the schema but `null` in
  every row. A shelfmark identifies a specific extant document; publishing one
  alongside a species assignment would disclose an unpublished research finding
  about a named object.
- **Real collection and provenance values.** Replaced with obviously fictional
  placeholders (`Collection A`, `Example Abbey`).
- **Sample identifiers.** `EXAMPLE_001…006`, not the real ones.
- **Species determinations.** The taxa here are inputs to a generator, not
  findings. Which animal any real relic label is made from is the project's
  result to publish.

The schema keeps `shelfmark` as a column precisely because the real one needs it
— demonstrating the field without populating it is the point.

### Encoding note

The real dataset's `shelfmark` values were briefly reported as mojibake. They are
not: the column holds the correct U+00E8 character and no replacement characters.
The apparent corruption was a terminal rendering artifact. See Finding 3a of the
[conformance audit](../../docs/conformance_audit_2026-09-08.md) -- kept there as a
note on how *not* to check encodings.
